evals.prompt: I want to learn Rust. I've been writing Go for 3 years so I'm not new to systems programming, but I've never touched Rust.
evals.expected_output: A docs-first mentorship compass for Rust that acknowledges the user's Go background, makes ownership and borrowing the first mental-model layer, and points to official Rust sources without turning rustlings or Rust By Example into mandatory exercises.

assertions.text: Uses the Mentorship Compass / Learning Compass structure with 4-5 iterations, not a 4-phase syllabus
Mentions ownership or borrowing in the Why This Topic Is Tricky section
Assumptions section reflects the user's Go background
First iteration starts with official conceptual Rust documentation, not setup or a quickstart
Any GitHub repository is framed as Inspect or Practice later, not clone/run/complete
No mandatory commands, install steps, clone steps, or required exercises
Includes Checkpoints, Avoid for Now, and Next Topics sections
Does not ask clarifying questions because the user gave clear context

evals.prompt: learning path for Google Cloud Run
evals.expected_output: A mentorship compass for Google Cloud Run that starts with the service model, uses official Google Cloud documentation first, distinguishes Cloud Run from Cloud Functions and GKE, and reserves quickstarts or deployment commands for later practice.

assertions.text: Uses Learning Compass iterations rather than Phase 1 / Phase 2 / Phase 3 / Phase 4 headings
Majority of compass resources are Tier 1 official Google Cloud docs
Why This Topic Is Tricky mentions confusion with Cloud Functions, GKE, or generic container hosting
No mandatory deploy commands, gcloud commands, install steps, or setup checklist
Quickstart material, if included, is marked Practice later or Skim for context rather than Read first
No resource appears in both Learning Compass and Explore Later

evals.prompt: I need to get up to speed on Karate DSL for API testing at work. We use it with Maven and run tests in CI pipelines.
evals.expected_output: A docs-first compass for Karate DSL that reflects Maven and CI usage, uses the official Karate documentation and repository, and points the learner to inspect relevant docs and repo areas instead of generating a Maven tutorial.

assertions.text: References the official Karate GitHub repository or official Karate documentation
Acknowledges that official docs are README-based or monolithic if it uses non-Tier-1 sources
Assumptions reflect Maven and CI context
Does not ask clarifying questions because the user gave clear context
No mvn commands, sample test implementation steps, or CI pipeline recipes unless marked Practice later

evals.prompt: Give me the best learning path for Terraform modules.
evals.expected_output: A narrow-topic mentorship compass that uses 2-4 iterations, starts with where modules fit in Terraform, uses official HashiCorp docs first, and distinguishes reading, inspection, bookmarks, and later practice.

assertions.text: Uses compressed Learning Compass iterations, not the full 4-phase model
Learning Compass has between 2 and 4 iterations
Includes at least one resource with mode Bookmark
Official HashiCorp docs appear before registry browsing or tutorials
No terraform commands, module creation checklist, or required hands-on tutorial in the main compass
No resource appears in both Learning Compass and Explore Later

evals.prompt: I want to learn React Server Components without wasting time on outdated articles.
evals.expected_output: A compass that asks one clarification question about framework context (Next.js, Remix, or raw React), gives a provisional default if useful, applies freshness rules, prefers current official docs, and avoids old tutorial content.

assertions.text: Asks exactly one clarification question about framework context
Provides or clearly offers a provisional default path if assuming Next.js App Router
Avoid for Now warns against outdated pre-stable or framework-mismatched RSC content
No resources older than 2023 unless they are still canonical
Includes Why This Topic Is Tricky mentioning documentation lag, fast-moving ecosystem, or framework-specific behavior
No app-building steps, npm/npx commands, or required project walkthrough in the main compass

evals.prompt: Teach me Cloud Run in 2 hours. I'm already a platform engineer.
evals.expected_output: A compressed mentorship compass optimized for orientation in a short time budget, assumes platform-engineer background, and points to the few docs that establish the right model without producing a weekend curriculum.

assertions.text: Learning Compass has between 2 and 3 iterations
Assumptions section reflects 2-hour time budget and platform engineer level
Explore Later is reduced or absent
Does not ask clarifying questions because the user gave clear context
No Phase 4 / Go Deeper heading
No mandatory quickstart, deploy command, or setup sequence

evals.prompt: What's the best way to learn GitLab CI caching?
evals.expected_output: A narrow-topic compass focused on one workflow area, using exact GitLab documentation pages and telling the learner what to notice about cache keys, paths, policy, and artifacts without writing a pipeline tutorial.

assertions.text: Uses compressed Learning Compass iterations
Learning Compass has between 2 and 4 iterations
Links to specific GitLab CI caching documentation pages, not the GitLab CI homepage
Includes What to notice and Stop before guidance for each iteration
No YAML implementation recipe, pipeline snippet, or commands unless explicitly marked Practice later

evals.prompt: I want a learning path for Astro (the web framework). I'm a React developer looking to build content-heavy sites.
evals.expected_output: A mentorship compass that uses official Astro docs where available, bridges conceptual gaps with maintainer or reputable sources when justified, and adapts the reading lens to a React developer building content-heavy sites.

assertions.text: Uses official Astro documentation where available
Includes explicit justification for any non-Tier-1 source
Does not pretend all official docs are complete if they are not
Assumptions reflect React background and content-heavy site goal
Does not ask clarifying questions because the user gave clear context
No npm create commands, starter setup sequence, or build-a-site tutorial in the main compass

evals.prompt: Give me a mentorship compass for Docker in JSON format. I'm a backend developer.
evals.expected_output: A valid JSON object conforming to references/schema.json with all required fields populated, using the broad-topic compass structure for Docker.

assertions.text: Output is valid JSON, not markdown
Includes all required top-level fields: topic, topic_scope, assumptions, why_this_topic_is_tricky, learning_compass, explore_later, checkpoints, avoid_for_now, next_topics, navigators_note
Every learning_compass iteration includes iteration, focus, read_first, check_next, inspect, what_to_notice, and stop_before fields
Every resource includes source_tier, mode, title, url, and why_here_now
mode values match the enum defined in schema.json and do not include Hands-on

evals.prompt: I understand the Docker docs basics. Now give me hands-on practice ideas.
evals.expected_output: A response that may include Practice later or hands-on suggestions because the user explicitly asked for practice, while keeping those activities separate from docs-first reading guidance.

assertions.text: Allows practice suggestions because the user explicitly requested hands-on practice
Keeps practice material separate from any docs-first compass
Still avoids low-quality generic tutorials and uses official or reputable sources
